That is the known idle dip this host takes below the 1,200 MHz lock floor, not a fault: re-asserting -lgc 1200,2500 brought SM back to 1,192 MHz within about two seconds and cleared the throttle flags to 0x0, confirmed over four consecutive samples. Recorded rather than silently corrected because attempt 2's abort turned on exactly this kind of reading being available afterwards.
gpu_preflight.observation_vram_baseline: nvidia-smi reads 21,224 MiB used with the np2 service up and idle and NO sidecar anywhere, on both the Windows host and inside WSL. That is the no-sidecar baseline attempt 2 measured (21,254-21,288 MiB during its own pre-miss window), and it is the figure the offline bridge's VRAM-return check is written against: a ceiling of 22,500 MiB proves the sidecar's roughly 2,837 MiB device allocation is gone before Pass B starts. UNLIKE attempt 2's preflight the weights are NOT evicted this time, so the canary's first prompt evaluation should not pay a re-page cost.

trace_isolation.flush_order: canary (own sink) -> PASS A (own sink, flushed before the bridge) -> offline bridge (no decoder trace) -> PASS B (main sink FIRST) -> resend (own sink)
trace_isolation.why_pass_a_is_namespaced: both passes emit an agent-loop runtime record per sample under the same record base, so Pass A flushes into its OWN namespaced sink and only Pass B -- the pass in which the policy actually decides -- lands in the main sink

coresidency_invariant.enforcement: two independent probes -- the launcher's own live sidecar handle and a TCP reachability probe of the embedder port -- asserted before EVERY frozen-core contact and at every phase boundary, fail-closed
coresidency_invariant.invariant: the CPU embedder sidecar is NEVER resident while a frozen-core decode contact is in flight

two_pass.design: PASS A flies all 104 contact-0 direct decodes with the embedder sidecar DOWN and runs NO policy; an OFFLINE BRIDGE embeds every uncovered Pass-A text with the sidecar UP ALONE and stops it with its own receipt; PASS B runs the frozen v1 cell over each trajectory's OWN flown text and flies only the evidence contacts the policy dispatches, resuming contact 0 from Pass A's durable record at zero core contacts. Deferral, never omission: the policy is never run against an inert or substituted query vector

dispatch_projection.flown_corroboration: attempts 1 and 2 together flew 86 BLEND trajectories and produced 86 direct-decode contacts and ZERO evidence-decode contacts
dispatch_projection.limitation: Pass A re-flies the direct decode. The program's known multi-slot decode-variance channel means a minority of flown texts will not reproduce the M0 text byte for byte (attempt 1: 4 of 26; attempt 2: 5 of 58). Where the text diverges the dispatch decision may differ, so this is a PROJECTION over the same population under the same policy, not a prediction of the flown count. The registered attempt ceiling carries a margin on top of it.
dispatch_projection.mechanism: content-facet cosines are healthy (all 104 above tau) but ALL 104 trajectories have ZERO content facets in the top-m rank window the fuser admits over, because the ranker's prior-mass dimensions score well above any cosine; percept admission reads only NON-prior-mass dimensions, so nothing is admitted and nothing is selected

m0_source.texts_verified_against: per-sample direct_response_sha256 in the M0 arm's own mechanical records

durable_query_vector_table.semantics: an embedding is a deterministic function of its text and every attempt-2 spawn proved bit-identical jitter numerics against the first spawn, so a vector already computed for a text on this row IS the vector the bridge would recompute. Reusing them is a serving cache and spends ZERO tool contacts. NOTHING is embedded before takeoff and no sidecar is spawned before Pass A.

offline_bridge.design: the ONE window in which the sidecar may exist: the GPU decode loop is stopped, the sidecar is spawned ALONE, every Pass-A text not already covered by the durable table is embedded in one batched session, and the sidecar is stopped with its own receipt before Pass B is allowed to start

sidecar_stop.reason: offline bridge complete -- Pass B flies with the sidecar DOWN

pass_a.design: the BLEND arm's OWN contact 0, flown with the embedder sidecar DOWN through the degenerate direct-decode-only controller whose initial_contact is byte-identical to the blend controller's. The policy is NOT run here: an inert query vector would change what the policy reads, so the decision is DEFERRED to Pass B, never omitted

pass_b.design: the REAL frozen v1 blend controller over the vector of THAT trajectory's OWN flown Pass-A text; contact 0 is RESUMED from Pass A's durable record and costs zero core contacts, the evidence contact wherever the policy dispatches is real and metered

replay.semantics: PASS B resumes each trajectory's contact 0 from Pass A's durable record rather than re-flying it; the sha256 of the messages document is proved equal to Pass A's on every single replay
